cohort: 3098 mothers of macrosomic babies (>4000g) who delivered between 2000-2015 at the study institution
finding: Predicted fetal macrosomia was associated with a higher cesarean section rate but a lower risk of postpartum hemorrhage, composite maternal adverse outcomes, and composite neonatal adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was more than 3.5 times higher in the group of predicted macrosomia (47.2% vs. 12.7%, P < 0.001) than those with unpredicted macrosomia.
